thread:
samir (oncall): FYI getting a customer escalation — p99 for /v1/generate in us-east1 jumped to ~3.2s around 17:06 UTC :rotating_light:

lina (sre): looking now, any error spikes or auth failures?
marta (support): customer report: high tail latency for inference calls, started ~17:05, they see timeouts and a couple 504s. No auth errors in their logs.
samir (oncall): metrics: host-level CPU/GPU fine, but TLS handshake p99 moved from ~40ms -> ~1.8s for a subset of requests.
zack (netinfra): did we change any egress weights or GSLB configs? routing-bot: recent GSLB weight change detected: us-east1 -> weight bump to legacy-edge-2 at 17:03 by auto-scale-policy.
lina (sre): that aligns. If traffic got shifted to legacy-edge-2 it may be introducing cross-zone hops. Can someone share traceroutes from affected customers?
marta (support): pasted redacted trace from customer (they're in us-east-1 AZ a):
```
traceroute to edge.redwood.com (52.19.13.7), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.3 ms  0.2 ms  0.2 ms
 2  isp-peering  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.1 ms
 3  core-isp  2.5 ms  2.6 ms  2.7 ms
 4  legacy-edge-2.us-east1  1800 ms  1795 ms  1794 ms
```

samir (oncall): huge hop to legacy-edge-2 — looks like an anycast drift / routing to an out-of-region host.
zack (netinfra): that 1.8s is likely the observed TLS handshake tail. Legacy-edge-2 has a known handshake warmup issue with long TCP/TLS renegotiation when certain peering paths are used.
lina (sre): can we confirm with internal probes? routing-bot: probe results (last 5m): us-east1->legacy-edge-2 avg tls_handshake=1.7s p99=2.1s; us-east1->primary-edge avg=60ms p99=120ms.
marta (support): customer is asking for ETA; they are on a paid Dedicated plan but using hosted endpoints.
samir (oncall): immediate mitigation suggestions?
lina (sre): 1) Short-term: adjust GSLB weights to favor primary-edge and decrease weight to legacy-edge-2 (manual override). 2) Mid-term: reduce DNS TTL for us-east1 entries to avoid sticky routing if we need rollbacks. 3) Longer: patch legacy-edge-2 TLS stack or remove it from pool if unstable.
zack (netinfra): I'll roll weight change now. Command: `gslbctl set-weight legacy-edge-2.us-east1 10` and `gslbctl set-weight primary-edge.us-east1 90`
deply-bot: noted: change request queued, staged to prod.

lina (sre): also enable route-level fallback so requests hitting legacy-edge-2 automatically re-route after a 2s handshake timeout — we have that policy but it was set to 3s in us-east1; lowering to 2s helps.
zack (netinfra): changing fallback threshold: `routingctl set-fallback-threshold us-east1 2s`
samir (oncall): applied weight change and lowered threshold. Monitoring...

(3m pass)
routing-bot: metrics update: us-east1 p99 dropped from 3.2s -> 180ms, TLS-handshake p99 -> 130ms.
marta (support): relay to customer: temporary routing adjustment made, tail latency should be normalized; will follow up if they still see issues.
lina (sre): capture PCAPs for a few legacy-edge-2 nodes for postmortem, and open a ticket to investigate handshake renegotiation path. Assign to netinfra.
zack (netinfra): created ticket NET-2431 "legacy-edge-2 TLS renegotiation under certain peering paths" and tagged with priority P1.
samir (oncall): whats the rollback plan if weight change causes other regressions? lina (sre): revert weights to previous values and set TTL back once stable. Keep manual locks in place to prevent auto-policy flip for next 30m.

marta (support): customer replied: saw improvement after ~2m, thanks. Asked for root cause and timeline for permanent fix.
lina (sre): we'll include remediation plan: 1) keep legacy-edge-2 at reduced weight until patch; 2) run e2e handshake tests across major ISPs; 3) patch TLS stack and validate in canary; 4) gradually restore weight.
zack (netinfra): quick repro steps for triage: 1) from affected ISP, run `curl -v --resolve edge.redwood.com:443:52.19.13.7 https://edge.redwood.com/v1/health` 2) monitor `openssl s_client -connect 52.19.13.7:443 -servername edge.redwood.com -msg` 3) collect handshake timings and retransmits.
samir (oncall): assign followups — zack owns NET-2431, lina will own postmortem and customer-facing summary, samir will keep oncall watch for 2 hours.
lina (sre): postmortem checklist: include timeline, GSLB weight history, routing-bot diffs, traceroutes, PCAP, plan for TTL change, and write regression test.
marta (support): I'll send interim note to customer and schedule a 1:1 if they want deeper writeup.
zack (netinfra): note: we should also audit auto-scale policy that bumped legacy-edge-2 weight — looks like rule mis-evaluated capacity. File AUTO-OPS-78.

samir (oncall): thanks team. tagging #postmortems when we have the draft. I'll keep this thread pinned for the next sync. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: change `gslbctl weight` applied by zack at 17:09 UTC (change-id: ch_78b2)

lina (sre): last check (17:23 UTC) client p99 holding ~140ms, no new alerts. closing incident, will open postmortem doc.
marta (support): customer confirmed resolution, closing ticket on their side.
samir (oncall): resolved for now. follow-ups: NET-2431, AUTO-OPS-78, postmortem doc by lina.
